title: Learned decoding validates a photonic receiver on a recorded transition trace
summary: Six learned decoders were fine-tuned on 1,502 recorded transitions from a phase-aware photonic receiver. Their voting ensemble classified 98.31% of 1,363 transitions in the immediately subsequent held-out trace. This is a specific retrospective physical-readout validation under the tested drift conditions, without a matched superiority comparison against the separate analytical decoder.
ai_technology: XGBoost; LightGBM; CatBoost; random forest; Extra-Trees; neural network

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, physical readout context, learned decoding Section6 and Tables1–2, conclusion; later-version context separately checked

evidence.tested: Physics-based synthetic pretraining followed by recorded-trace fine-tuning and an immediately subsequent experimental test trace. Learned features comprise normalized output-power differences and the preceding decoded state.
evidence.unknown: Back-to-back traces may share drift and hardware conditions. Sequential inference requires a previous-state reference and limited drift. No independently acquired locked-model deployment, energy, latency, network benefit or unrestricted phase-noise robustness was established. The receiver design and separate 96.19% analytical result are not credited to AI.
evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers map measured receiver power changes plus the preceding state to the next codeword, enabling the reported held-out physical readout evaluation.
